name: The Archmage's Spire
realm: The final climb. Many scrolls become one great work.
lesson: Real programs span many files. Declarations (class bodies, function prototypes) go in headers (.hpp) guarded with #pragma once; definitions go in .cpp files. The compiler builds each .cpp separately and the linker joins them - 'undefined reference' means something was declared but never defined. Prefer RAII and smart pointers so cleanup is automatic.

trial.prompt: What prevents a header from being included twice?
Definitions usually live in which kind of file? (extension)
static class members belong to the ___ not each object. (one word)
trial.explain: One copy for the whole class.

options: a) pastes the header text in
a) let members manage themselves so you write no special member functions
boss.explain: Use RAII members; defaults just work.

spell.prompt: CAPSTONE: build class Spellbook in two files. spellbook.hpp declares it with void add(const std::string&) and int count() const (plus a private vector<string>); spellbook.cpp defines both functions.
spell.hint: class Spellbook { public: void add(const std::string& s); int count() const; private: std::vector<std::string> spells; };  then  void Spellbook::add(...) { spells.push_back(s); }
spell.explain: Headers declare, sources define, the linker joins.
